skills.name: Buttons & Badges
skills.summary: The action vocabulary: button variants and sizes, loading/disabled contracts, icon buttons with names, and badge/status chips.

sections.definition: Buttons and badges are the action vocabulary of an interface: buttons commit actions (primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive), badges label state (status chips, counts, categories). The craft is a closed variant system - every button variant has a documented hierarchy role, size ramp, and state set (hover/active/focus/disabled/loading) - so products compose actions instead of redesigning them.
principles: One primary per view: the primary variant marks the single most-likely action; competing primaries dissolve hierarchy.
Variants are hierarchy, not decoration: primary (filled), secondary (outline), tertiary (ghost), destructive (danger-filled) - each has a documented use contract.
Sizes come from the ramp: sm 32px, md 40px, lg 48px heights; touch surfaces meet 44px minimum (a11y 2.5.8).
Loading replaces label with spinner + 'Processing': the button stays sized (no reflow), disabled, and announces via aria-live.
Disabled is styled AND explained: tooltip or helper text says why - a bare disabled button is a dead end.
Icon-only buttons have accessible names: aria-label minimum; visible tooltip recommended - icon alone is never the name.
Badges carry status triples: color + icon + text (a11y 1.4.1); count badges cap at 99+; dot badges pair with screen reader text.
Destructive actions confirm or undo: destructive buttons either open a confirmation or ship an undo path - never a single-click delete.

tokens.notes: Closed variant set; no ad-hoc buttons
Count badges cap; overflow reads as 99+

composition: Composes with skill-design-tokens: button colors, radii, and spacing consume semantic/alias tokens - buttons never hardcode values.
Composes with semantic-color-system (skill-color-theory guide 06): destructive and status badges consume status ramps.
Composes with forms-inputs (guide 02): submit buttons and input heights share the size ramp.
patterns: Button component contract: one component exposing variants x sizes x states, with the loading/disabled/announcement behavior implemented once.
Badge role matrix: badges map to status/label/count categories, each with its signal triple and overflow behavior documented.
useCases: Any product UI: forms, toolbars, cards, dialogs all consume the button system.
Design systems: buttons are usually the first component built - the contract sets the pattern for the rest.
Audit: competing primaries, icon buttons without names, unexplained disabled states.
antiPatterns: Two primaries: filled CTA next to filled CTA - the eye picks neither
Icon-only mystery buttons: unlabeled glyph buttons screen readers read as 'button'
Reflow loading: button shrinking to a spinner and shifting the layout
Dead-end disabled: greyed actions with no explanation of what unlocks them

accessibility.notes: Buttons are WCAG 2.1.1/2.4.7/2.5.8 territory: real <button> elements, visible focus, 44px touch floors, and loading announced via aria-live - icon-only controls carry accessible names (a11y repo guides 03/05).
accessibility.fallback: If a custom button variant cannot meet the state contract (loading/announce), ship the native button with the closest variant - native semantics beat custom styling without states.

skills.name: Forms & Input Recipes
skills.summary: Text fields, selects, checkboxes, and validation layouts: the label-hint-error wiring recipe and forgiving-validation timing.

sections.definition: Form inputs are the highest-traffic, highest-stakes components: text fields, selects, checkboxes, radios, switches, and their validation choreography. The recipe is structural, not cosmetic: visible labels wired programmatically, hints via aria-describedby, errors flagged with aria-invalid, and validation timing that forgives mid-typing - the same wiring the a11y repo mandates, expressed as a component recipe.
principles: Visible labels always: placeholder-only inputs are banned - labels persist above or beside the field (WCAG 3.3.2).
The wiring recipe: label-for + hint-describedby + error-describedby + aria-invalid - implemented once in the field component, consumed everywhere.
Input heights match the button ramp: 40px default, 48px on mobile forms - a form is one rhythm.
Validation timing: validate on blur or submit; inline errors clear on fix; never per-keystroke scolding.
Errors state cause + fix: 'Enter a valid email like name@domain.com' - the message content is part of the recipe (ux-writing guide 08).
Choice controls are honest: checkbox = independent toggles, radio = exclusive pick, switch = instant-effect setting - semantics match behavior.
Disabled vs readonly are distinct: disabled removes from tab order (and needs explanation); readonly stays focusable and copyable.
Autocomplete attributes ship: name/email/tel autofill (WCAG 1.3.5) is part of the recipe, not a nice-to-have.
composition: Composes with buttons-badges: submit/primary actions share the size ramp and loading contract.
Composes with forms-errors (skill-accessibility guide 07): that guide owns the WCAG criteria; this recipe implements the component.
Composes with ux-writing (skill-ux-writing): label and error phrasing follow the voice & tone and error message guides.
patterns: Field component with slots: one Field wrapper owns label/hint/error/error-flag wiring; inputs plug in - wiring drift becomes impossible.
Error summary on submit: failed submits focus a linked error list at top + per-field inline messages (a11y repo pattern).
useCases: Any form: signup, checkout, settings, search.
Design systems: the field component is the second component built (after button).
Audit: placeholder-labels, unwired errors, per-keystroke validation noise.
antiPatterns: Placeholder-as-label: hints vanishing on first keystroke
Unwired errors: red borders with no aria-invalid or text association
Keystroke scolding: 'invalid' firing mid-typing before the user finishes
Mixed control semantics: switches that submit forms, checkboxes that act instantly

accessibility.notes: The recipe implements WCAG 3.3.1-3.3.5, 1.3.5, and 4.1.2 at the component level: programmatic labels, described-by wiring, forgiving timing, and autofill - a11y repo guide 07 owns the criteria, this recipe ships the mechanics.
accessibility.fallback: If the field wrapper cannot be adopted repo-wide, ship the wiring checklist per form (label-for, describedby, invalid, summary) - the wiring is the deliverable, the wrapper is the convenience.

skills.name: Tables & Data Grids
skills.summary: Sortable, filterable, paginated tables: column semantics, sticky headers, selection models, and the grid-vs-table decision.

sections.definition: Data tables are where information density and interaction meet: sorting, filtering, pagination, row selection, and inline editing. The recipe distinguishes a table (read data; native <table> semantics) from a grid (interactive cells; ARIA grid pattern) - and covers column types (numeric right-aligned tabular, actions as menus), sticky headers, and empty/loading states as first-class table states.
principles: Table vs grid is a semantics decision: read-only data stays a native <table>; per-cell interactive editing becomes an ARIA grid - never a div-soup of either.
Real <table> semantics: th scope, caption, thead/tbody - screen reader navigation (a11y repo aria-fundamentals) depends on it.
Column types have contracts: numeric right-aligned + tabular figures (typography guide 10), text left-aligned, actions as kebab menus, timestamps relative-with-absolute-title.
Sorting announces: aria-sort on column headers; sort buttons meet the 44px target floor.
Selection models are explicit: none, single, multi - with select-all that respects filter scope and announces selection count.
Sticky headers for long tables: position-sticky th persists context on scroll (responsive-layout guide 09 owns mobile adaptation).
Empty and loading are table states: zero-results with a recovery suggestion; skeleton rows that preserve column alignment.
Pagination is honest: counts ('1-25 of 1,204'), page size controls, and URL-persisted state - fake-infinite tables lose users' place.

tokens.notes: Column headers persist on vertical scroll

composition: Composes with responsive-layout guide 09: that guide owns narrow-screen adaptation; this recipe owns features and semantics.
Composes with data-viz-palettes (skill-color-theory guide 08): status coloring inside tables follows the CVD-safe viz rules.
Composes with numeric-tabular (skill-typography guide 10): tabular figures + alignment are shared contracts.
patterns: Table kit: one Table component family (Table, Column, RowActions, Pagination) with the semantic/sticky/sort contracts implemented once.
Column contract declarations: columns declare type (numeric/text/action/date) and the kit applies alignment, figures, and menu treatment automatically.
useCases: Admin and enterprise surfaces where tables are the primary object.
Finance/analytics products with comparison-critical data.
Audit: div-tables, hover-only actions, fake pagination, unwired sorting.
antiPatterns: Div-table soup: CSS-grid divs where screen readers need th/td semantics
Hover-only actions: row toolbars invisible to touch and keyboard
Sort-by-invisibility: sorted columns with no aria-sort or visual direction cue
Pagination theater: 'infinite' tables that reset scroll and lose user place

accessibility.notes: Tables implement WCAG 1.3.1 (structure), 2.1.1 (keyboard-sort/actions), and the ARIA grid pattern when interactive: scope/caption semantics, aria-sort, and keyboard-reachable row actions are the recipe's non-negotiables.
accessibility.fallback: If the full grid pattern is too heavy for a surface, ship the native table with keyboard-reachable actions (menus open via keyboard) - a semantic table with menus beats a partial grid.

skills.name: Modals & Dialogs
skills.summary: The dialog contract done once: role/label, focus trap-and-return, Escape, scrim, and the when-NOT-to-modal decision table.

sections.definition: Modal dialogs interrupt flow for a focused task: confirmations, short forms, critical notices. The recipe is the full dialog contract - role=dialog, accessible name, focus trap-and-return, Escape/scrim close, scroll lock, and stacked-dialog handling - implemented once in a Dialog primitive. Equally important is the decision table of when NOT to modal: most confirmations belong inline or as toasts; modality is for tasks that must complete before proceeding.
principles: Modal earns its interruption: use for confirmation of destructive/irreversible actions, focused subtasks, and blocking notices - everything else is inline or a toast.
The contract is uniform: role=dialog + aria-modal + labelled-by title, focus enters on open, traps inside, returns to trigger on close (a11y repo guide 04).
Escape and scrim both close (except blocking): destructive-task dialogs keep Escape dismissible with confirmation - blocking alerts document the exception.
Scroll lock without layout shift: body scroll locks with scrollbar-width compensation - the page must not jump when the dialog opens.
Dialogs are short: one task, one primary action, one escape hatch - multi-step flows are routes or wizards, not nested modals.
Stacking is capped and ordered: dialog-on-dialog is capped at 2 with managed focus order; 3+ signals the flow needs redesign.
Size variants by task: sm (confirmations), md (short forms), lg (content-heavy) - with mobile behavior declared (full-screen sheet under 640px).
Native <dialog> where possible: the platform element carries focus management and :modal styling - the primitive builds on it.

tokens.notes: Enter on open, return to trigger

composition: Composes with forms-inputs: dialog forms use the field recipe; dialog buttons use the button contract.
Composes with focus-management (skill-accessibility guide 04): that guide owns the focus criteria; this recipe implements the dialog around them.
Composes with toasts-notifications: post-dialog feedback lands as a toast - dialogs close, confirmation narrates politely.
patterns: Dialog primitive: one component (native <dialog>-based) exposing size variants, the focus contract, and scrim/escape handling - every modal composes it.
When-to-modal decision table: confirmation/subtask/blocking vs inline/toast/route - reviewed at design time, not built time.
useCases: Destructive confirmations (delete, revoke, transfer).
Focused subtasks (invite member, edit record) that must finish or abort.
Audit: modal fatigue, trap-less dialogs, scroll-jump on open, 3-deep stacking.
antiPatterns: Modal fatigue: everything in a modal until users reflex-click through the one that mattered
Trap-less dialogs: focus escapes to the dead page behind the scrim
Focus-to-nowhere: dialogs that close and drop focus to body
Scroll-jump opens: scrollbar loss shifting the whole page sideways

accessibility.notes: Dialogs implement the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern: role/name/trap/escape/return are the five non-negotiables (a11y repo guides 03/04) - a dialog missing any one is a build failure in review.
accessibility.fallback: If the trap implementation cannot be completed, use the native <dialog> element with showModal() - it carries the focus contract natively.

skills.name: Toasts & Notifications
skills.summary: Transient feedback done politely: aria-live narration, timing that respects reading speed, stacking, and the undo pattern.

sections.definition: Toasts deliver post-action feedback without stealing focus: 'Saved', 'Invitation sent', 'Item archived - Undo'. The recipe covers the politeness contract (aria-live=polite, focus never stolen), timing (4-8s scaled by content length, dismissible, paused on hover), stacking limits, and the undo pattern that replaces confirm dialogs for reversible actions. Bad toasts are noise; good toasts are the feedback layer.
principles: Toasts never steal focus: they narrate via aria-live=polite - focus stays where the user is (a11y 4.1.3).
Timing scales with content: 4s minimum, +1s per extra line, 8s cap; errors persist until dismissed - users read at their own pace.
Dismissible + hover-pause: every toast has a close control and pauses its timer on hover/focus - auto-dismissal never outruns a screen reader.
The undo pattern beats confirmation: 'Archived - Undo' replaces confirm dialogs for reversible actions (a11y cognitive-content contract).
Max 3 stacked: older toasts collapse into a digest or a notification center - a toast column is not a feed.
Placement is consistent and non-blocking: bottom-right (desktop) / top (mobile) over content, never covering the action just performed.
Success is quiet, error is loud: success toasts are subtle; error toasts persist, pair with an icon, and link to the fix.
Notifications have a home: high-volume products route history to a notification center/drawer - toasts are the ephemeral layer only.

tokens.notes: Never assertive for success; focus never stolen
Undo action window for reversible actions
History lives in a dedicated surface

composition: Composes with buttons-badges: undo/close actions inside toasts use the button contract.
Composes with modals-dialogs: the when-to-modal table routes reversible actions to toasts-with-undo instead of confirm dialogs.
Composes with feedback-confirmation (skill-animation): toast entrance/exit uses motion tokens; reduced-motion collapses it (a11y).
patterns: Toast service: one app-level toast manager owning queue, stack cap, placement, and the polite live region - components call toast(), never build their own.
Undo-first flow: reversible actions skip confirmation entirely and announce 'done - Undo' - the confirmation budget is reserved for the irreversible.
useCases: Post-save/post-send feedback in any app.
Destructive-but-reversible actions (archive, remove from list).
Audit: toast floods, unreadable auto-dismiss, toasts covering the button just clicked.
antiPatterns: Toast flood: every action toasting until the stack is a feed nobody reads
Speed-read dismissal: 2s toasts vanishing before the text registers
Assertive success: aria-live=assertive interrupting the user for 'Saved'
Blocking placement: toasts covering the button the user just clicked

accessibility.notes: Toasts implement WCAG 4.1.3 (status messages): polite narration without focus theft, durations a screen reader user can meet (hover-pause), and dismissal controls - the toast service is a11y infrastructure, not decoration.
accessibility.fallback: If a toast cannot be announced (legacy stack), pair critical feedback with an inline status region on the page - narration must exist somewhere, even if not transient.

skills.name: Navigation Patterns
skills.summary: Top bars, sidebars, breadcrumbs, and pagination: the wayfinding components, current-page semantics, and responsive collapse contracts.

sections.definition: Navigation components are the wayfinding layer: top bars (identity + global actions), sidebars (section nav with collapsible groups), breadcrumbs (hierarchy location), tabs-as-nav, and pagination. The recipe covers each pattern's structure, the current-page contract (aria-current + visual marker), keyboard behavior, and responsive collapse (sidebar → drawer per responsive-layout guide 08).
principles: Nav landmarks structure the page: header/nav/main/footer landmarks with one main - the page skeleton ships as a template (a11y repo aria-fundamentals).
Current page is semantic + visual: aria-current=page plus a visual marker - both, always (a11y 1.4.1).
Sidebars declare depth and grouping: collapsible sections with aria-expanded; depth capped at 3 - deeper IA is restructured, not nested.
Breadcrumbs for hierarchy, back for flow: breadcrumbs show where you are in a hierarchy; back buttons/links handle task flow - never confuse them.
Skip links are part of nav: the nav block ships with the skip-to-content link as one template.
Keyboard paths are nav contracts: menu triggers, drawer toggles, and breadcrumb links are all keyboard-operable with visible focus.
Pagination for archives, load-more for feeds: pagination preserves place (URL state); infinite feeds need a 'jump to top' escape.
Responsive collapse is declared: sidebar → drawer, top bar → bottom bar - the collapse contract is written with the component (responsive-layout guide 08).

tokens.notes: Separators decorative; nav is the list
Skip link ships with nav template
Collapse behavior is written, not discovered

composition: Composes with responsive-layout guides 01/08: the shell grid and mobile collapse contracts are shared documents.
Composes with keyboard-navigation (skill-accessibility guide 03): skip links, landmarks, and keyboard paths are the a11y layer of this recipe.
Composes with dropdowns-menus (guide 09): nav overflow items collapse into the menu pattern.
patterns: Nav template kit: header + sidebar + breadcrumbs + skip link as one composable template - pages assemble wayfinding, never rebuild it.
Current-page contract: one helper resolves aria-current + visual marker across top bar, sidebar, and breadcrumbs from the same route state.
useCases: App shells for dashboards and admin tools.
Documentation/marketing sites with hierarchical nav.
Audit: no aria-current, breadcrumbs-as-back-buttons, sidebar depth spirals.
antiPatterns: Current-page guesswork: users lost because active nav state is a subtle tint
Breadcrumb-as-back: hierarchical crumbs used for task flow back-navigation
Depth spiral: 5-level sidebar nesting nobody can hold in memory
Nav rebuild per page: every page hand-rolling its header instead of consuming the template

accessibility.notes: Navigation implements WCAG 1.3.1/2.4.1/2.4.5-2.4.8: landmarks, skip links, current-location semantics, and consistent placement - the nav template is the accessibility skeleton of the product.
accessibility.fallback: If a full sidebar cannot be keyboard-perfect in time, ship the flat top-nav variant - a simple, complete keyboard path beats a rich, broken one.

skills.name: Cards & Lists
skills.summary: Content containers: card anatomy, list-item patterns, media-object rows, and the whole-card-clickable done accessibly.

sections.definition: Cards and list items are the content containers of every feed, dashboard, and catalog: a card bundles media, title, meta, and actions into one composable unit; a list row does the same in compact form. The recipe covers card anatomy (header/body/media/footer slots), the media-object row pattern, hover/elevation contracts, and the whole-card-clickable pattern done accessibly (one link, stretched, with named actions preserved).
principles: Card anatomy is slotted: media, title, meta, body, actions - the card component owns slots, content decides what fills them.
One action per card, visually primary: a card may hold multiple actions, but exactly one is the primary link - the card's identity action.
Whole-card-clickable without nested links: the primary link stretches over the card (pseudo-element), while other buttons sit above it (z-index) - no link-in-link markup.
Media-object rows for repeating content: avatar/icon + text + trailing action as one shared pattern (responsive-layout guide 04).
Elevation is a state language: resting cards sit flat (border), hoverable cards lift - elevation changes mean interactivity, nothing else.
List rows keep rhythm: 48-72px row heights, dividers or spacing (never both), and consistent trailing-action alignment.
Card grids inherit the layout system: cards are content; the grid (responsive-layout guides 01/05) decides their geometry.
Titles are the semantic anchors: card titles are headings in context (h2/h3 level in the page outline) - not styled divs.

tokens.notes: Titles are real headings in context
Geometry from responsive-layout, not card CSS

composition: Composes with responsive-layout guides 04/05: media-object and grid geometry are shared contracts.
Composes with buttons-badges: card actions consume the button/badge contract.
Composes with skill-ui-ux styles: card styling (radius, elevation, borders) is where design styles surface most - styleAffinity records the lean.
patterns: Card component with anatomy slots: one card primitive; products compose media/title/actions into catalog, dashboard, and feed variants.
Stretched-link recipe: primary link with ::after covering the card; interactive children raise above it - accessible whole-card clicking without nested links.
useCases: Feeds, catalogs, and dashboards (every product has a card somewhere).
Notification lists, search results, and settings groups as list rows.
Audit: nested interactive markup, hover-only affordances, styled-div titles.
antiPatterns: Link-in-link markup: a whole clickable card containing buttons - invalid HTML, broken AT
Everything-lifts: elevation on static cards until lift means nothing
Divider-and-spacing: double separation reading as heavy-handed noise
Styled-div titles: card titles outside the page heading outline

accessibility.notes: Cards are a hot spot for 1.3.1/2.4.4/4.1.2: single-link semantics (stretched pattern), real headings, and named actions - the stretched-link recipe exists specifically to make whole-card clicking compatible with AT.
accessibility.fallback: If the stretched pattern is unavailable, make only the title a link with a clearly-sized hit area - a smaller clickable is better than invalid nesting.

skills.name: Tabs & Accordions
skills.summary: Disclosure widgets per APG: tabs for peer views, accordions for progressive detail - roles, keyboard maps, and the choice rule.

sections.definition: Tabs and accordions are disclosure widgets: they swap or reveal content while keeping page structure. Tabs present peer views of one object (manual selection per APG); accordions progressively reveal detail within a page (details/summary or button+region). The recipe covers the APG contracts - roles, roving tabindex, aria-expanded/selected - and the decision rule: tabs switch peers, accordions condense, and navigation-style tabs are links instead.
principles: Tabs for peers, accordions for detail: tabs switch between peer views of one object; accordions reveal optional depth - misusing tabs as content condensing buries content.
APG tabs contract: role=tablist/tab/tabpanel, roving tabindex with arrow keys, Home/End, aria-selected - the keymap is the standard (a11y repo guide 06).
Accordion = button + expanded region: native details/summary when styling allows; otherwise button with aria-expanded + region - the trigger is always a real button.
Panels are labelled: tabpanel labelled by its tab; accordion regions labelled by their trigger - AT users hear where they landed.
One open accordion is the default: multiple-open needs a reason (comparison tasks) - single-open keeps scroll position stable.
URL state for tab views: peer views that bookmark/refresh (tab=usage in URL) - state users can link to.
No lazy surprises: tab panel content mounts on demand but announces loading; content must not shift the page when revealed.
Never tabs inside tabs inside accordions: nesting disclosure widgets beyond one level is a content-architecture failure.

tokens.notes: Site navigation is links, not tabs

composition: Composes with accessibility-wiring (guide 11) and a11y repo guide 06: the APG keymaps are shared contracts this recipe implements.
Composes with tables-data-grid and forms-inputs: tab panels host full recipes; disclosure widgets are containers, not content.
Composes with skill-animation entrance-exit: panel transitions use motion tokens; reduced-motion collapses them instantly.
patterns: Disclosure kit: Tabs and Accordion components implementing the APG contracts once - products compose panels, never re-implement keymaps.
Peer-content review: content designed for tabs passes the 'would a user expect this as a peer view?' test at design time - buried-content checks before build.
useCases: Product detail views (overview/specs/reviews), settings groups, and docs.
FAQs, release notes, and help panels as accordions.
Audit: div-tabs, auto-activating arrows, accordion content invisible to find-in-page.
antiPatterns: Div-tabs: clickable divs with no roles or keymaps
Auto-activation chaos: panels swapping on every arrow pass - disorienting and slow
Buried content: primary content stuffed in tab 3 where find-in-page and print cannot see it
Accordion-everything: whole pages as accordions - scroll lost, content hidden

accessibility.notes: Disclosure widgets are APG territory (a11y repo guide 06): roles, roving tabindex, expanded/selected states, and labelled panels - a tab widget that narrates nothing is decoration, not a widget.
accessibility.fallback: Where the full tab contract cannot ship, use native radio-style selection or plain sections with anchor links - semantic structure beats partial widgets.

skills.name: Dropdowns & Menus
skills.summary: Selects, menus, popovers, and tooltips: the value-vs-action distinction, keyboard contracts, and positioning that stays in viewport.

sections.definition: Dropdown-family components divide into value pickers (select, combobox - choose a value) and action menus (dropdown menu, context menu - trigger a command), plus the popover/tooltip satellites. Confusing them is the classic bug: a menu-as-select breaks form narration and mobile behavior. The recipe covers each pattern's contract, keyboard map, positioning (floating-ui, viewport-aware flip/shift), and the native-select default.
principles: Value vs action is the first decision: choosing a value = select/combobox; triggering a command = menu - the distinction drives semantics and keymaps.
Native select is the default: unless styling demands more, <select> carries mobile pickers, autofill, and AT support for free.
Menus are APG-exact: role=menu/menuitem, arrows navigate, Escape closes, focus returns to trigger - invented keymaps break muscle memory (a11y repo guide 06).
Combobox = input + listbox: aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant or focus-managed options, typeahead, and announced result counts.
Positioning never clips: floating positioning with flip/shift keeps popovers in viewport - overflow: hidden ancestors are tested, not assumed.
Tooltips are hover supplements, never the only label: dismissible, hoverable, persistent (WCAG 1.4.13) - and the control carries its own accessible name.
Popovers escape their DOM box: position: fixed/absolute rendering (top layer) so parent overflow/stacking contexts cannot clip them.
Nested menus are capped: one submenu level; deeper IA becomes a dialog or page - depth 3 menus are unusable on touch.
composition: Composes with forms-inputs: combobox/select are form fields - the field wiring recipe wraps them.
Composes with accessibility-wiring and a11y repo guide 06: APG menu/combobox contracts are the AT layer of this recipe.
Composes with navigation-patterns: nav overflow collapses into menus; the menu contract is shared.
patterns: Popover primitive: one positioning wrapper (floating-ui) powering menus, tooltips, and popovers - flip/shift/escape logic implemented once.
Native-first audit: every custom dropdown in the codebase justifies itself against <select>/<details> - custom pickers need custom features to exist.
useCases: Toolbars and row actions (kebab menus).
Filtered pickers (country, user, tag comboboxes).
Audit: menu-as-select, clipped popovers, tooltip-only labels.
antiPatterns: Menu-as-select: role=menu picking form values - narration and mobile pickers break
Clipped popovers: menus amputated by overflow: hidden ancestors
Tooltip-only labels: icon buttons whose name lives only in hover
Submenu spirals: three-deep cascades unusable by keyboard and touch alike

accessibility.notes: This recipe implements the APG menu/combobox/listbox patterns plus WCAG 1.4.13 (tooltip contract): keymaps, focus return, announced results, and dismissible tooltips - dropdown family is where invented keymaps do the most damage.
accessibility.fallback: When a custom picker cannot complete its APG contract, ship the native select - a plain-looking select that works beats a beautiful one that narrates nothing.

skills.name: Command Palette & Search
skills.summary: Cmd-K overlays: fuzzy search over actions and objects, keyboard-first UX, recent/frecency ranking, and the analytics loop.

sections.definition: The command palette (Cmd-K) is the power-user surface: one overlay searching across actions ('Create project'), navigation ('Go to settings'), and objects ('Open ACME deal'). The recipe covers the overlay contract (modal focus, trap-and-return), the search index (actions + objects + navigation), fuzzy matching, frecency ranking, and the analytics loop that records which commands run - palettes are data products as much as UI.
principles: One palette, three item types: actions, navigation, objects - the index is typed and each type renders a distinct group with a distinct verb.
Keyboard-first contract: Cmd-K/Ctrl-K opens, arrows navigate, Enter runs, Escape closes - mouse is the fallback, not the target.
Fuzzy matching with typeahead: matching tolerates typos and abbreviations ('usr set' finds User Settings) - strict prefix matching starves palettes.
Frecency + recency ranking: recently/frequently used items surface first - the palette learns the user.
Empty state teaches: a first-run palette shows examples ('Try: create, invite, export') - the blank palette is a dead end.
Dialog contract underneath: the palette is a dialog - focus trap, return, Escape, scroll lock (guide 04 recipe) all apply.
Results are announced: result counts narrate politely as the user types (combobox contract).
Analytics close the loop: query logs with no-result tracking feed the index - 'nothing found' entries are roadmap data.
composition: Composes with modals-dialogs: the overlay contract (trap/return/Escape/scrim) is the dialog recipe.
Composes with navigation-patterns: 'Go to...' items make the palette a navigation accelerant on top of the nav system.
Composes with dropdowns-menus: the result list follows the combobox contract (announced counts, activedescendant).
patterns: Typed command registry: features register actions into the palette index with (type, verb, keywords, handler) - palette coverage grows with features automatically.
No-result analytics: weekly review of zero-result queries; missing commands become tickets - the palette's index is maintained like a search engine's.
useCases: Power-user products: IDEs, CRMs, project tools, admin consoles.
Deep-IA products: palettes flatten navigation for large apps.
Audit: palettes missing actions, strict matching, no analytics.
antiPatterns: Silent palettes: overlays that grab focus and narrate nothing
Strict matching: 'proj cr' finding nothing while the user stares
Static ranking: every query returning the same order - the palette never learns
Actionless palettes: navigation-only palettes where users expected verbs

accessibility.notes: The palette is the keyboard-accessibility showcase: it IS a keyboard-only interface, so the dialog + combobox contracts must be airtight - focus management, narration, and Escape behavior are its core features, not polish.
accessibility.fallback: If analytics/fuzzy search cannot ship in v1, launch with a static typed list + arrow/enter keyboard contract - a simple, narrated palette beats a broken search.

skills.name: Empty, Loading & Error States
skills.summary: The states most components forget: skeletons that match layout, empty states that teach, error states that recover.

sections.definition: Every component has more states than its happy path: loading (first load, refetch, inline), empty (first-use, no-results, cleared), and error (network, permission, not-found). Products fail here most visibly - a blank box communicates nothing while a designed empty state onboards. The recipe covers skeleton discipline, empty-state taxonomy with next actions, and error-state recovery paths.
principles: Skeletons match the final layout: the skeleton is the component's own geometry - a generic spinner-less gray blob that swaps into a different shape causes a jarring shift.
Never skeleton past 3 seconds: long loads switch to progress indication (bar, percentage) - skeletons are for sub-3s waits.
Empty states are taxonomy-driven: first-use (teach + CTA), no-results (relax the query suggestion), cleared (restore action) - each has its own copy and action.
Empty states carry the next action: 'Create your first project' with the button - an empty state without an action is a dead end.
Errors are specific and recoverable: what failed, why (in user terms), and the recovery action (retry, contact, alternative path).
Offline is a designed state: detect and message degraded connectivity with the retry contract - not a browser error.
Permission errors explain the unlock: 'Ask your admin for access' with the request action - not a bare 403.
All states are announced: loading/empty/error narrate via live regions or focus moves (a11y repo guide 04) - state changes AT users can hear.

tokens.notes: Empty states carry the next action
Every error has a path forward
Recipes ship with all states designed

composition: Composes with every recipe in this repo: each component's spec includes its loading/empty/error states - states are part of the recipe.
Composes with toasts-notifications: async failures land as persistent toasts with retry; inline errors stay in-component.
Composes with ux-writing (skill-ux-writing): empty/error copy follows the voice/tone and error-message guides.
patterns: State triad per component: every recipe ships (loading, empty, error) alongside default - a component without its triad is an incomplete spec.
Error taxonomy: network/permission/not-found/validation each get their approved copy pattern - engineers pick from the taxonomy, not from scratch.
useCases: First-run experiences: empty states are the onboarding surface.
Async-heavy dashboards: loading and error choreography.
Audit: blank boxes, skeleton-to-content layout jumps, bare 403s.
antiPatterns: Blank-box states: unstyled empty/loading/error surfaces shipping to production
Skeleton-forever: spinners-as-skeletons hanging past 3s with no progress
Dead-end errors: 'Something went wrong' with no cause and no path
Layout-jump loads: skeleton geometry that doesn't match the content it becomes

accessibility.notes: State changes are WCAG 4.1.3 surface: loading/empty/error transitions announce politely, error focus moves to summaries (forms contract), and empty-state CTAs are keyboard-reachable - states designed without AT are half-designed.
accessibility.fallback: If a live-region announcement cannot be wired for a state, move focus to the state's heading instead - focus movement is the fallback narration channel.

skills.name: Component A11y Wiring
skills.summary: The cross-cutting a11y layer every recipe shares: focus contracts, announcements, target sizes, and reduced-motion - checked per component.

sections.definition: Every recipe in this repo shares one wiring layer: keyboard operability, focus contracts, live announcements, target sizes, contrast through tokens, and reduced-motion behavior. Rather than repeating it twelve times, this guide is the component-level a11y checklist: the per-component pass that verifies the recipe's accessibility wiring before it ships - the bridge between the a11y repo's criteria and this repo's components.
principles: Every recipe ships its a11y wiring: the component spec includes keyboard map, focus behavior, announcements, and target size - not an appendix.
Keyboard map before styling: each component declares its keymap (per APG where applicable) before pixels - the map is the spec.
Focus contracts per surface: what receives focus on open/expand/select, what returns on close/collapse - per component, tested per state.
Announcements are designed: state changes users must hear (loading done, error, selection) wire to live regions or focus moves deliberately.
44px touch targets are the floor: all interactive surfaces meet the effective-target minimum (2.5.8) - dense variants use spacing, not smaller targets.
Contrast comes from tokens: component colors consume validated alias pairs (design-tokens/skill-color-theory) - components never introduce unvalidated colors.
Reduced-motion is wired per component: entrance/exit/loading motion collapses under prefers-reduced-motion (skill-animation guide 12) - the component owns its fallback.
The checklist runs per component, per PR: the wiring pass is a review gate - components merge only with the checklist green.

tokens.notes: Live region or focus move, deliberate
Keyboard pass first, then screen reader

composition: Composes with every recipe here: this guide is the shared checklist they all reference.
Composes with skill-accessibility guides 03/04/05/06: the criteria layer this wiring implements at component level.
Composes with skill-design-review: the design-side review consumes this checklist as its component section.
patterns: The wiring checklist block: a standardized checklist (keymap, focus, announce, target, contrast, motion) pasted into every component's spec and PR template.
Wiring-first reviews: PRs touching components route to reviewers who run the checklist - a11y review is scheduled, not aspirational.
useCases: Design systems: the gate every new component passes before publishing.
Component audits: scoring existing components against the wiring checklist.
Onboarding engineers: the single page that teaches component-level a11y.
antiPatterns: A11y-as-appendix: wiring considered after styling, patched in at review
Checklist theater: boxes ticked without running the keyboard pass
Style-first specs: component specs with no keymap or focus section
Unvalidated colors: one-off hex values inside components escaping the token system

accessibility.notes: This guide exists to make component-level accessibility systematic: the per-component checklist operationalizes WCAG 2.1.1, 2.4.7, 2.4.13, 2.5.8, 4.1.3, and 1.4.3 across every recipe - the checklist is the deliverable.
accessibility.fallback: When a component cannot pass the full checklist, it does not ship as a shared primitive - it ships as an app-local component with documented gaps, keeping the system clean.
